verdict.rationale: Aider directly supports the checks half of the story: it lints edited files by default, runs tests via /test or automatically with --test-cmd/--auto-test, and runs code via /run. The diff half is weaker. Aider commits each edit with an '(aider)'-tagged descriptive message so changes can be reviewed in git history, but diff inspection relies on git rather than a documented dedicated diff view. missing for 10: a documented first-party diff inspection/review command or view, explicit pre-merge workflow guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the lint/test checks.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect diffs and run checks to catch problems before merging

citations.quote: By default, aider will lint any files which it edits.
You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
Whenever aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message. This makes it easy to undo or review aider's changes.
Go back in the git history to review the changes that aider made to your code
